options.why: Divided the run by the rise instead of the rise by the run.
Used the rise of $24$ on its own without dividing by the run of $8$.
Quoted the $y$-intercept of the line instead of its gradient.

questions.solution_text:
The line passes exactly through $(1, 8)$ and $(9, 32)$.
$b = \frac{32 - 8}{9 - 1}$
$= \frac{24}{8}$
$= 3$

options.why: Counted the rise in grid squares ($6$ squares up over $10$ across) instead of reading the axis labels, where each vertical square is $10$ umbrellas.
Counted the vertical intercept as $3$ grid squares instead of reading its label of $30$ umbrellas.
Read both the intercept and the gradient in grid squares, never converting either using the vertical scale of $10$ umbrellas per square.

questions.solution_text:
The line passes exactly through $(0, 30)$ and $(10, 90)$.
$b = \frac{90 - 30}{10 - 0}$
$= \frac{60}{10}$
$= 6$
The line crosses the vertical axis at $30$, so $a = 30$.
$u = 30 + 6r$

questions.question_text:
A council fits the line of best fit $L = 58.3 + 2.15n$, where $L$ is the number of litres of water used per person per day and $n$ is the number of hot days in the week.
Which statement interprets the gradient correctly?

options.text: For each extra hot day in the week, water use per person is predicted to rise by $2.15$ litres per day.
The gradient is $2.15$.
options.why: States the number without saying what it means in the context or giving its units.

options.text: For each extra litre of water used, the number of hot days is predicted to rise by $2.15$.
options.why: Interprets the rate the wrong way round, treating $L$ as the independent variable.

options.text: For each extra hot day in the week, water use per person is predicted to rise by $58.3$ litres per day.
options.why: Uses the $y$-intercept as the rate of change instead of the gradient.

questions.solution_text:
The gradient is $2.15$, the change in $L$ for a one-unit increase in $n$.
Water use per person rises by $2.15$ litres per day for each extra hot day in the week.

questions.question_text:
A study of second-hand tractors gives the line of best fit $P = 96\,400 - 6800h$, where $P$ is the price in dollars and $h$ is the number of thousands of hours the tractor has been used.
Which statement interprets the gradient correctly?

options.text: The predicted price falls by $\$6800$ for each extra thousand hours of use.
The predicted price rises by $\$6800$ for each extra thousand hours of use.
options.why: Ignores the negative sign of the gradient, so the direction of change is reversed.

options.text: The predicted price falls by $\$96\,400$ for each extra thousand hours of use.
options.why: Uses the $y$-intercept as the rate of change instead of the gradient.

options.text: A tractor used for $6800$ hours is worth nothing.
options.why: Treats the gradient as a number of hours rather than a change in price per thousand hours.

questions.solution_text:
The gradient is $-6800$, the change in $P$ for a one-unit increase in $h$.
The predicted price falls by $\$6800$ for each extra thousand hours of use.

questions.question_text:
A gym's monthly bill follows the line of best fit $B = 39 + 7.5v$, where $B$ is the bill in dollars and $v$ is the number of visits in the month.
Which statement interprets the $y$-intercept correctly?

options.text: A member who makes no visits is still billed $\$39$, which is meaningful as a fixed monthly membership fee.
Each visit adds $\$39$ to the bill.
options.why: Reads the $y$-intercept as the rate of change, which is the gradient.

options.text: A member who makes no visits is billed $\$7.50$.
options.why: Substitutes $v = 0$ but reports the gradient rather than the constant term.

options.text: A member who makes no visits is billed $\$46.50$.
options.why: Adds the gradient to the intercept instead of substituting $v = 0$.

questions.solution_text:
The $y$-intercept is $39$, the value of $B$ when $v = 0$.
A member who makes no visits is billed $\$39$.
Zero visits is possible and the fee is a real fixed charge, so the intercept is meaningful here.

questions.question_text:
For a group of adults, the line of best fit is $S = 14.6 + 0.58h$, where $S$ is shoe size and $h$ is hand length in centimetres.
Which statement interprets the $y$-intercept correctly?

options.text: A person with a hand length of $0$ cm would have shoe size $14.6$, which is not meaningful because nobody has a hand length of $0$ cm.
A person with a hand length of $0$ cm would have shoe size $14.6$, which is meaningful because $14.6$ is a possible shoe size.
options.why: Judges the intercept by whether the $y$ value looks plausible rather than by whether $x = 0$ can occur.

options.text: Shoe size rises by $14.6$ for each extra centimetre of hand length.
options.why: Reads the $y$-intercept as the rate of change, which is the gradient.

options.text: A person with shoe size $0$ would have a hand length of $14.6$ cm.
options.why: Sets the dependent variable to zero instead of the independent variable.

questions.solution_text:
The $y$-intercept is $14.6$, the value of $S$ when $h = 0$.
A person with a hand length of $0$ cm would be predicted to have shoe size $14.6$.
A hand length of $0$ cm is impossible and no such person was in the data, so the intercept has no meaning here.

questions.question_text:
A line of best fit is written as $y = 5.9x + 48$.
Which pair of values is correct?

options.text: Gradient $5.9$, $y$-intercept $48$
Gradient $48$, $y$-intercept $5.9$
options.why: Reads the two numbers in the order written rather than by their role in the equation.

options.text: Gradient $5.9$, $y$-intercept $-48$
options.why: Changes the sign of the constant term when rewriting the equation as $y = a + bx$.

options.text: Gradient $53.9$, $y$-intercept $0$
options.why: Adds the two coefficients together instead of keeping them separate.

questions.solution_text:
$y = 5.9x + 48$
$= 48 + 5.9x$
The constant term is the $y$-intercept, so $a = 48$.
The number multiplying $x$ is the gradient, so $b = 5.9$.

questions.question_text:
For a bivariate dataset the line of best fit has gradient $-0.35$ and crosses the vertical axis at $73$.
Which equation is correct?

options.why: Uses the gradient as the constant term and the intercept as the coefficient of $x$.
Drops the negative sign of the gradient.
Makes the intercept negative because the gradient is negative.

questions.solution_text:
The $y$-intercept is the constant term, so $a = 73$.
The gradient is the coefficient of $x$, so $b = -0.35$.
$y = 73 - 0.35x$
